label: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database (Human Ageing Genomic Resources, build 15)
governance: Curated by a single academic group (Human Ageing Genomic Resources, J. P. de Magalhaes lab). Entries are compiled from the primary literature and personal communications; curation policy is described in the release notes. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (legal.html, checked 2026-10-31). No per-build DOI; the requested citation is a Nucleic Acids Research database paper (release.html asks for Tacutu et al. 2013, NAR 41(D1):D1027-D1033; the 2024 HAGR update is de Magalhaes et al., NAR 52(D1):D900-D908).
versioning: Numbered builds. The species index page states 'Build 15 (03/07/2023): 4,671 entries' and release.html states 'Release date: July 3, 2023', 'Number of entries: 4,671'. The zipped dataset (anage_data.txt, 31 columns) contains 4,645 data rows, i.e. 26 fewer than the stated entry count; the difference is not explained in the release notes. The download URL is unversioned (dataset.zip always serves the latest stable build), so the recorded SHA-256 identifies the build only until the next release.
known_issues: Entry count mismatch: site and release notes say 4,671 entries, the distributed anage_data.txt has 4,645 rows (re-derived 2026-10-31; build 15 zip SHA-256 matched the vendored records).
Unversioned download URL: dataset.zip is overwritten at each build, so checksums will stop matching when build 16 is released.
Vendored records cite three different NAR papers (gks1155 2013, gkx1042 2018, gkad927 2024); release.html requests gks1155, so gkx1042 is a real HAGR paper but not the requested citation.
Taxonomy in the file is older than the project's accepted names (e.g. Neovison vison rather than Neogale vison), so binomial matching against current names undercounts.
rationale: Peer-reviewed database papers in NAR and explicit builds justify a high but not maximal authority score: the dataset has no DOI and the release notes contradict the file's own row count. Independence is moderate because AnAge is a literature compilation that shares its underlying sources with PanTHERIA and the Amniote Life-History Database rather than reporting primary measurements. Authenticity is high: the DOIs resolve to the papers they claim, the licence page says CC BY 3.0, and the file contents re-downloaded 2026-10-31 reproduce the vendored checksums and per-taxon row counts.
